sentences.text: Radhakrishnan vs State Of Kerala on 9 January, 2025

Bench: J.K. Maheshwari, Aravind Kumar
 In The Supreme Court Of India
 Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction
 Criminal Appeal No. 1996 Of 2014
 Radhakrishnan Appellant(s)
 Versus
 State Of Kerala Respondent(s)
 O R D E R

1) Arising out of the judgment of conviction and sentence for the charges under Sections 376 and 450 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, directing the appellant to undergo sentence of seven years and three years respectively, confirmed by the High Court, the present appeal has been filed.

2) After going through the testimony of the victim, statement of the Doctor and the findings by which the High Court do not find the plea of alibi plausible and reliable, in the facts and circumstances of the case and after hearing learned counsel for the parties, we do not find any ground Reason: sentence as awarded.

CRIMINAL APPEAL NO. 1996 OF 2014 3) The appellant was released on bail by this Court as per order dated 12.09.2014; however, he is directed to surrender within a period of four weeks to serve the remaining part of the sentence,
otherwise the trial Court shall take steps for taking him into custody for serving the sentence.
Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.
5) Copy of this order be sent to the Court concerned.

., J.
[ J.K. MAHESHWARI ] ., J.
[ ARAVIND KUMAR ] New Delhi;
January 09, 2025.

HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE J.K. MAHESHWARI HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE ARAVIND KUMAR
For Appellant(s) Mr. Renjith B. Marar, Adv. Mr. Renjith. B, AOR Mr. Arun Poomulli, Adv. Ms. Lakshmi N. Kaimal, Adv.

For Respondent(s) Mr. C. K. Sasi, AOR Ms. Meena K Poulose, Adv.
UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following O R D E R 1) The criminal appeal stands dismissed in terms of the signed order.

Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.
